copy.blurb:
A +6.5pp gap on the the draw side. Germany v Curaçao in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has the draw stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

The Elo prior reads Germany 1900 vs Curaçao 1480: 420 points in favour of Germany, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Germany to win at 83%, the draw at 10%, and Curaçao to win at 7%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. the draw on the win side reads 10%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Germany to win at 94%, the draw at 4%, and Curaçao to win at 3%. On the the draw side specifically the market reads 4%, which prices out at American odds of +2717. Compared against the model's 10%, that's the +6.5pp gap the Pick rests on.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On the draw, that haircut lands the model at 10%; the market is at 4%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +6.5pp. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 23 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page. Two outlets covered the build-up this week — BBC Sport (football): "Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer comes out of international retirement to be named in Germany's squad for the 2026 World Cup, with…"; The Guardian (football): "Yes I plan with [Neuer as No 1]"
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives the draw a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +6.5pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

copy.summary: The model and the market disagree on whether a stalemate is in play here. Our prior puts the draw at 10%; Polymarket prices it at 4%. The +6.5pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Germany v Curaçao · the model leans the draw
